items.title: Nidana Panchaka
items.english: Five means of understanding a disease
items.summary: Classical diagnosis rests on five components that together describe how a disease arises and shows itself. Every condition article in this encyclopedia is organised around them.

head: Component
Meaning
rows: Causes: diet, lifestyle, season, external factors
Early warning signs before the disease is fully expressed
Diagnostic response: what relieves or aggravates (a therapeutic test)
Pathogenesis: how the disturbed dosha travels and lodges

p: Samprapti is summarised by its components (Ghataka): the dosha involved, the tissues affected (Dushya), the channels (Srotas), the type of channel disturbance, the seat of disease (Adhishthana), the state of Agni and whether Ama is present. Condition articles show these in Doctor and Student views.

items.title: Rogi and Roga Pariksha
items.summary: Classical texts describe several structured examination systems. In modern practice they complement, never replace, clinical examination and investigations.

sections.h: Dashavidha Pariksha (tenfold assessment of the patient)
list: Satmya: habituation, what suits the person
Ahara Shakti: capacity to take and digest food

p: Pulse reading appears in later texts (Sharangadhara Samhita; Yogaratnakara) rather than in Charaka or Sushruta. Studies of agreement between practitioners and of diagnostic accuracy are few and inconsistent. Pulse reading must not replace blood pressure measurement, ECG, laboratory tests or imaging when these are indicated.

Many classical conditions overlap with diseases that need laboratory confirmation: blood sugar and HbA1c for Prameha/diabetes, haemoglobin for Pandu/anaemia, liver tests for Kamala/jaundice, thyroid tests, urine examination, imaging for stones. Ayurvedic Standard Treatment Guidelines (Ministry of AYUSH) also recommend relevant modern investigations.
